projects.title: Scout in production: tested, traced, budgeted and load-tested
projects.goal: Turn Scout into a pip-installable service with unit tests, cassette tests, evals, OpenTelemetry-style logs, cost caps and human approval, then prove it under 50 concurrent conversations with p50/p95/p99 numbers.
steps: Package Scout as `scout/` with a `pyproject.toml`, a pinned model id in `config.toml`, and the `search_notes`, `calculator` and `write_file` tools behind a registry.

Write at least 12 pytest unit tests against a scripted FakeModel covering the step limit (max 8 steps), a tool that raises, parallel tool results in one message, and a per-run budget of 20,000 tokens.
Record 10 real conversations as cassettes with secrets scrubbed (authorization, x-goog-api-key) and replay them in CI so the full suite runs in under 30 seconds with no key.
Build a 25-case golden set with a scorer, run each case 5 times, and report pass@1 and pass@5 plus the per-case flake rate.
Emit one JSON line per step with gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, run id, stop reason, tool name, latency and cost, with emails and phone numbers redacted.
Gate `write_file` behind an approve/edit/reject prompt that writes an audit record (who, when, arguments, decision) to `audit.jsonl`.
Run 50 conversations concurrently with a semaphore of 10 and a shared token bucket, and report p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per run, 429 count and retries.
Kill the load test mid-run, resume from checkpoints, and show no `write_file` call ran twice.
projects.deliverable: A GitHub repo with a green CI badge, `make test` and `make load` targets, and a README containing the eval table (pass@1, pass@5), the latency/cost table for 50 concurrent runs, one annotated trace of a failed run, and the resume-without-duplicates proof.
stretch: Export the JSON-line spans to a local Jaeger or Grafana Tempo via the OpenTelemetry SDK and include a screenshot of one full run trace.
Add small-model-first routing (escalate to the bigger model only on a failed scorer check) and report cost saved against eval pass-rate lost.
Make the eval suite a required CI check that fails a pull request if pass@1 drops by more than 5 points.

projects.title: Multi-provider LLM gateway with failover and capacity plan
projects.goal: Build the small internal gateway a platform team puts in front of every agent: one API over Gemini, a local Ollama model and a fake, with per-team keys and quotas, circuit-breaker failover, and a capacity and cost plan for 5,000 users.
steps: Expose a FastAPI `/v1/chat` endpoint backed by the provider-neutral adapter, with Gemini as primary, a local Ollama model (e.g. qwen3 small) as secondary and a FakeModel for tests.
Issue per-team gateway keys read from environment or a secret file, enforce a per-team token bucket (e.g. 60 requests/min, 200,000 tokens/day) and return 429 with retry-after when exceeded.
Add a circuit breaker per provider that opens after 5 failures in 30 seconds, fails over to the secondary, and half-opens after 60 seconds.
Drive 20 requests/second for 10 minutes with a load script, inject a 3-minute primary outage (500s and timeouts from a stub server), and record error rate and p95 latency before, during and after.
Never retry 400-class or spend-cap 429 errors; prove it with a test for each error type and log request ids for every upstream call.

Write a capacity model for 5,000 users (assume 20 runs/user/day, 6 steps/run, 3,000 input and 400 output tokens/step): peak tokens per minute against provider tiers, concurrency via Little's law, the effect of a 70% cache-hit rate, 2x burst headroom and monthly cost.
projects.deliverable: A repo with the gateway, the outage drill script, and a README with a chart of error rate and latency across the outage window, the measured time-to-failover, and the capacity spreadsheet or notebook with its monthly cost estimate and assumptions.
stretch: Add a shadow mode that mirrors 5% of traffic to a candidate model and logs answer diffs without returning them to callers.
Containerise the gateway with Docker Compose (gateway, Ollama, stub server) so the outage drill runs with one command.

projects.title: Red-teaming a customer-support agent against prompt injection
projects.goal: Apply the attack catalogue to a different domain, a support-ticket agent that can look up orders, issue refunds and send email, and show with numbers how layered defences cut the attack success rate without hurting normal tickets.
steps: Build a support agent with tools `read_ticket`, `lookup_order`, `issue_refund(order_id, amount)` and `send_email(to, body)` over a fixture of 200 synthetic orders and 60 tickets.
Write 30 attacks: instructions hidden in ticket text, in order notes and in customer names, markdown-image exfiltration of other customers' emails, and confused-deputy refunds to a different order.
Write 30 benign tickets with expected actions as a utility set, and score both sets automatically from tool-call logs (not from the model's text).
Measure the baseline attack success rate and benign task success over 3 runs per case.

Add defences one at a time: untrusted content kept inside tool results, a tool permission matrix (refunds capped at the order total and $100), `send_email` limited to the ticket's own customer, and human approval for refunds over $50.
Report attack success rate, benign success rate and cost per ticket after each defence layer, and mark which attacks still get through and why (the lethal-trifecta check).
projects.deliverable: A repo with the agent, the attack and benign suites as JSONL, and a README with a defence-by-defence table of attack success, benign success and cost, plus three annotated transcripts of attacks that succeeded at baseline.
stretch: Add a second, cheaper model as an input classifier that flags suspected injections, and report its precision and recall on the 60 cases.
Run the full suite on two different models and compare their baseline susceptibility.

projects.title: Model migration canary for an invoice-extraction agent
projects.goal: Build the go/no-go pipeline a team runs before a pinned model retires: an invoice-processing agent, an eval set, and a canary report that diffs accuracy, tool-call behaviour, tokens, cost and refusals between the current and the candidate model.
steps: Build an agent that reads invoice text or PDFs, calls `lookup_vendor` and `convert_currency`, and returns a Pydantic-validated record (vendor, date, line items, total, currency).
Create 40 labelled invoices including 8 hard ones (multi-currency, missing totals, handwritten-style OCR noise) and a field-level scorer.
Pin the current model id in config and run the set 3 times to establish a baseline of field accuracy, schema-valid rate, tool-call rate, input/output tokens and cost per invoice.
Run the same set on a candidate model at two reasoning-effort levels and diff every metric, including refusals and the number of validation retries.
Route 10% of a replayed day of 500 invoices to the candidate as a canary and stop automatically if field accuracy drops more than 2 points or cost per invoice rises more than 20%.
Generate a one-page Markdown migration report with a recommendation, the retirement date of the current model and a rollback plan.
projects.deliverable: A repo with the agent, the labelled set, a `make canary MODEL=<id>` target and a README with the baseline-vs-candidate table (accuracy, valid-schema rate, tool-call rate, tokens, cost, refusals) and the generated migration report.
stretch: Add prompt caching of the stable system prompt and vendor table and report the measured cache-hit rate and cost change.
Send the 500-invoice backfill through a batch API and compare its cost and wall-clock time with the online run.
